title: PEPI: Dataset Structure and Notation
text: vignette intended introduce context notation used PEPI, inference framework quantify epigenetic dynamics longitudinal WGS data. Cells sorted according marker represents abstract phenotype, can either expressed (positive, ⊕\oplus) expressed (negative, ⊖\ominus). multiple time points, cells collected sequenced separately positive negative populations. goal PEPI quantify dynamics epigenetic states combining two sources information: Variant allele frequencies (VAFs) measured across genome sorted population. Longitudinal cell counts positive negative cells sampling time. PEPI leverages multivariate VAF spectrum together longitudinal counts infer switching rates states fitness clonal populations. allows distinguishing heritable (stable) epigenetic states plastic (unstable) states. detailed description underlying mathematical model, see: Integrating clonal evolution cell plasticity chronic lymphocytic leukaemia bimodal CD49d expression, preparation.

title: PEPI: Dataset Structure and Notation
text: PEPI, clades categorized based presence driver mutations relationship lineage structure. categories help model capture different evolutionary scenarios estimate fitness effects accurately. driver_n – driver mutation appears cells negative epistate (⊖) give rise detectable clade.Interpretation: mutation present cells, subclonal expansion small detect. PEPI uses model fitness effect driver without observing full clade expansion. dc – driver mutation associated observed nested clade.Interpretation: driver arose cell, descendants formed clade can traced lineage tree. PEPI treats driver clade, modeling impact clade growth epigenetic switching. cd – subclonal expansion nested within existing clade.Interpretation: new driver selective event occurs inside existing clade, creating nested pattern. PEPI uses capture subclonal heterogeneity interactions nested expansions. clade – wild-type clade, .e., clade without detected driver mutations.Interpretation: Represents background population cells evolve without selective drivers, used infer baseline epigenetic dynamics. Together, clade types allow PEPI distinguish driver-driven expansions epigenetic effects accurately model complex lineage structures bulk longitudinal data.

title: PEPI: Dataset Structure and Notation
text: PEPI works longitudinal datasets cells sorted marker represents abstract phenotype. marker can either expressed (positive, ⊕) expressed (negative, ⊖). multiple time points, cells collected whole-genome sequencing (WGS) performed separately positive negative cells. dataset PEPI contains three main components: muts – table mutations variant allele frequencies (VAFs) measured negative (⊖) positive (⊕) cells time point. row corresponds mutation, columns include VAFs different time points sorted populations. counts – longitudinal counts negative (⊖) positive (⊕) cells sampled time point. genomic_constants – contains mu (baseline mutation rate) genome_length (total length simulated genomic region; 51e6 bp datasets simulated chromosome 22). components assembled PEPI object following structure: $clade_statistics – summary clade-level statistics, including number mutations, VAFs, driver type, whether clade detected. $counts – observed counts negative positive cells. $genomic_constants – mutation rate (mu) genome length (genome_length). Two synthetic datasets included PEPI: Driver Example (no_driver_example) – system stable epigenetic state detectable driver mutations. Driver Example (driver_example) – system containing driver mutation associated detectable nested clade. datasets analyzed two dedicated vignettes (no_driver driver) illustrate package works. structure PEPI object consistent across datasets uses following nomenclature: cluster_name – identifier clade. driver_type – type driver associated clade (e.g., dc, cd, driver_n, empty wild-type clades). has_driver – logical indicating whether driver present. is_clade – logical indicating whether mutations form clade.

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: vignette illustrates complete analysis workflow using PEPI package. PEPI implements Bayesian framework quantifying epigenetic plasticity bulk genomic data longitudinal cell counts. analyze two datasets included package: no_driver_example: system strongly heritable epigenetic state rewind_example: system plastic (unstable) epigenetic state datasets simulated ProCess, cancer evolution simulator available https://github.com/caravagnalab/ProCESS. Cancer cells collected two time points sorted according epistate. subset cells, WGS simulated order obtain VAF coordinate time point epistate. : • visualize lineage tree • inspect VAF structure • fit PEPI epigenetic model • compare posterior estimates ground truth

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: Clear clustering VAF space reflects coherent clonal structure. observe particular cluster revealing expansion first clade. stability ⊕\oplus state reflected low VAF variable ⊖\ominus sample.
code: muts <- PEPI::no_driver_example$muts  get_branch = function(forest,cell_id,stop_id){      s = cell_id   branch = s      while(s > stop_id){          s =  forest %>% filter(cell_id == s) %>% pull(ancestor)     if(s > stop_id){branch = c(branch,s)}   }      return(branch)    } id = forest %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  ids = get_branch(forest,stop_id = 0,cell_id = id)  muts = muts %>% mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id %in% ids,"first clade",                                       ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal","subclonal")))   p1 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,common.legend = T)

code: pepi_obj <- get_posterior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables pepi_obj <- get_prior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables p_omega <- plot_inference(pepi_obj, parameter = c("omega_p"), log_scale = TRUE)  # Data frame for the line vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 2.5e-02)  # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping p_omega = p_omega +   geom_vline(data = vline_df,              aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),              linetype = "dashed") +   scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red")  p_s <- plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("s_epi"), log_scale = F)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_s = p_s +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )  ggarrange(plotlist = list(p_omega,p_s),nrow = 1,ncol = 2,common.legend = T)

text: VAF clade cluster high frequency samples, consistent state rewiring.

ifelse(cell_id %in% ids,"first clade",                                       ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal","subclonal")))   p1 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,           common.legend = T) m = muts %>% filter(label == pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables   clade_statistics <- tibble(       cluster_name = "S",       n_muts = m,       vaf_1_n = code: pepi_obj <- get_posterior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables pepi_obj <- get_prior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables p_omega <- plot_inference(pepi_obj, parameter = c("omega_p"), log_scale = TRUE)  # Data frame for the line vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 2.5e-02)  # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping p_omega = p_omega +   geom_vline(data = vline_df,              aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),              linetype = "dashed") +   scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red")  p_s <- plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("s_epi"), log_scale = F)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.2)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_s = p_s +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )      p_n <- plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("omega_n"), log_scale = T)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.5)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_n = p_n +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )  ggarrange(plotlist = list(p_omega,p_s,p_n),nrow = 1,ncol = 3,common.legend = T)

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: vignette illustrates complete analysis workflow using PEPI package. PEPI implements Bayesian framework quantifying epigenetic plasticity bulk genomic data longitudinal cell counts. analyze two datasets included package: no_driver_example: system strongly heritable epigenetic state rewind_example: system plastic (unstable) epigenetic state datasets simulated ProCess, cancer evolution simulator available https://github.com/caravagnalab/ProCESS. Cancer cells collected two time points sorted according epistate. subset cells, WGS simulated order obtain VAF coordinate time point epistate. : • visualize lineage tree • inspect VAF structure • fit PEPI epigenetic model • compare posterior estimates ground truth

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: Clear clustering VAF space reflects coherent clonal structure. observe particular cluster revealing expansion first clade. stability ⊕\oplus state reflected low VAF variable ⊖\ominus sample.
code: muts <- PEPI::no_driver_example$muts  get_branch = function(forest,cell_id,stop_id){      s = cell_id   branch = s      while(s > stop_id){          s =  forest %>% filter(cell_id == s) %>% pull(ancestor)     if(s > stop_id){branch = c(branch,s)}   }      return(branch)    } id = forest %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  ids = get_branch(forest,stop_id = 0,cell_id = id)  muts = muts %>% mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id %in% ids,"first clade",                                       ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal","subclonal")))   p1 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,common.legend = T)

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: object requires clade statistics (number mutations, ccf), total cell counts different time points genomic constants mutation rate genomic length.
code: m = muts %>% filter(label == "first clade") %>% nrow()  vaf = muts %>% filter(label == "first clade") %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf")) %>%    reshape2::melt() %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables   clade_statistics <- tibble(       cluster_name = "S",       n_muts = m,       vaf_1_n = vaf$vaf_1_n,       vaf_1_p = vaf$vaf_1_p,       vaf_2_n = vaf$vaf_2_n,       vaf_2_p = vaf$vaf_2_p,       is_clade = TRUE,       names = "first clade",       driver_type = "",       has_driver = FALSE,       rewind = FALSE )   times = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(sample) %>%    summarize(t = max(birth_time)) %>% pull(t) %>% sort()  counts = no_driver_example$counts  n_times = 2  c1 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[1] - 0.01 & time < times[1] + 0.01) c1 = c1[c(nrow(c1)-1,nrow(c1)),] c2 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[2] - 0.01 & time < times[2] + 0.01) c2 = c2[c(nrow(c2)-1,nrow(c2)),]  ztot  = c(c1 %>% pull(count) %>% sum(),c2 %>% pull(count) %>% sum())  rho_1 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_1") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_1_n = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_1_p = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  rho_2 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_2") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_2_n = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_2_p = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  zminus = c(ccf_1_n,ccf_2_n)*ztot zplus =  c(ccf_1_p,ccf_2_p)*ztot   counts <- tibble(   count_n = zminus,   count_p = zplus,   time = times )  mu = no_driver_example$mu$mean    genomic_constants <- tibble(   variable = c("genome_length", "mu"),   value = c(51e6, mu) )  pepi_obj = init(clade_statistics = clade_statistics,counts = counts,                 genomic_constants = genomic_constants)  pepi_obj #> $clade_statistics #> # A tibble: 1 × 11 #>   cluster_name n_muts vaf_1_n vaf_1_p vaf_2_n vaf_2_p is_clade names driver_type #>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <lgl>    <chr> <chr>       #> 1 S               275  0.0557   0.272  0.0617   0.251 TRUE     firs… ""          #> # ℹ 2 more variables: has_driver <lgl>, rewind <lgl> #>  #> $counts #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>    count_n count_p  time #>      <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1  360220. 101601.  8.30 #> 2 1633217. 474160.  9.30 #>  #> $genomic_constants #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   variable        value #>   <chr>           <dbl> #> 1 genome_length 5.10e+7 #> 2 mu            5.40e-7 #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "PEPI"

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: VAF clade cluster high frequency samples, consistent state rewiring.
code: muts <- PEPI::rewind_example$muts  id = forest %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  ids = get_branch(forest,stop_id = 0,cell_id = id)  muts = muts %>% mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id %in% ids,"first clade",                                       ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal","subclonal")))   p1 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,           common.legend = T) m = muts %>% filter(label == "first clade") %>% nrow()  vaf = muts %>% filter(label == "first clade") %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf")) %>%    reshape2::melt() %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = median(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables   clade_statistics <- tibble(       cluster_name = "S",       n_muts = m,       vaf_1_n = vaf$vaf_1_n,       vaf_1_p = vaf$vaf_1_p,       vaf_2_n = vaf$vaf_2_n,       vaf_2_p = vaf$vaf_2_p,       is_clade = TRUE,       names = "first clade",       driver_type = "",       has_driver = FALSE,       rewind = T )   times = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(sample) %>%    summarize(t = max(birth_time)) %>% pull(t) %>% sort()  counts = rewind_example$counts  n_times = 2  c1 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[1] - 0.01 & time < times[1] + 0.01) c1 = c1[c(nrow(c1)-1,nrow(c1)),] c2 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[2] - 0.01 & time < times[2] + 0.01) c2 = c2[c(nrow(c2)-1,nrow(c2)),]  ztot  = c(c1 %>% pull(count) %>% sum(),c2 %>% pull(count) %>% sum())  rho_1 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_1") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_1_n = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_1_p = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  rho_2 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_2") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_2_n = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_2_p = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  zminus = c(ccf_1_n,ccf_2_n)*ztot zplus =  c(ccf_1_p,ccf_2_p)*ztot   counts <- tibble(   count_n = zminus,   count_p = zplus,   time = times )  mu = rewind_example$mu$mean    genomic_constants <- tibble(   variable = c("genome_length", "mu"),   value = c(51e6, mu) )  pepi_obj = init(clade_statistics = clade_statistics,counts = counts,                 genomic_constants = genomic_constants)  pepi_obj #> $clade_statistics #> # A tibble: 1 × 11 #>   cluster_name n_muts vaf_1_n vaf_1_p vaf_2_n vaf_2_p is_clade names driver_type #>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <lgl>    <chr> <chr>       #> 1 S               505   0.242   0.336   0.269   0.339 TRUE     firs… ""          #> # ℹ 2 more variables: has_driver <lgl>, rewind <lgl> #>  #> $counts #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   count_n count_p  time #>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 269145.  98205.  13.3 #> 2 867063. 361651.  14.3 #>  #> $genomic_constants #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   variable        value #>   <chr>           <dbl> #> 1 genome_length 5.10e+7 #> 2 mu            1.05e-6 #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "PEPI"

title: PEPI: Inference example of epigenetic dynamics
text: compare ground truth inferred posterior distributions ω⊕\omega_\oplus, s⊕s_\oplus ωn\omega_n.
code: pepi_obj <- get_posterior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables pepi_obj <- get_prior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables p_omega <- plot_inference(pepi_obj, parameter = c("omega_p"), log_scale = TRUE)  # Data frame for the line vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 2.5e-02)  # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping p_omega = p_omega +   geom_vline(data = vline_df,              aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),              linetype = "dashed") +   scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red")  p_s <- plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("s_epi"), log_scale = F)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.2)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_s = p_s +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )      p_n <- plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("omega_n"), log_scale = T)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.5)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_n = p_n +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )  ggarrange(plotlist = list(p_omega,p_s,p_n),nrow = 1,ncol = 3,common.legend = T)

title: PEPI: Inference example with a subclonal expansion
text: Driver-associated mutations form high-VAF cluster. cluster reaches higher VAF ⊕\oplus sample , time driver emergence, ⊕\oplus population smaller, driver therefore expands competing fewer cells. also observe distinct cluster associated first nested clade within driver lineage.
code: muts <- PEPI::driver_example$muts  get_branch = function(forest,cell_id,stop_id){      s = cell_id   branch = s      while(s > stop_id){          s =  forest %>% filter(cell_id == s) %>% pull(ancestor)     if(s > stop_id){branch = c(branch,s)}   }      return(branch)    }  id_B = forest %>% as_tibble() %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  id_cl = forest %>% as_tibble() %>% filter(mutant == "B",epistate == "+") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  branch_dr = get_branch(forest,cell_id = id_B,stop = 0) branch_cl = get_branch(forest,cell_id = id_cl,stop = id_B)  muts = muts %>% mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id %in% branch_dr,"driver",     ifelse(cell_id %in% branch_cl,"first nested clade","subclonal"))) %>%   mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal",label))   p1 <- PEPI::plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- PEPI::plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,common.legend = T)

title: PEPI: Inference example with a subclonal expansion
text: object requires clade statistics (number mutations, ccf), total cell counts different time points genomic constants mutation rate genomic length.
code: m_clade = muts %>% filter(label == "first nested clade") %>% nrow() m_driver = muts %>% filter(label == "driver") %>% nrow()  vaf_clade = muts %>% filter(label == "first nested clade") %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf")) %>%    reshape2::melt() %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables  vaf_driver = muts %>% filter(label == "driver",cell_id == id_B) %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf"))%>%  reshape2::melt() %>% filter(value < Inf) %>%    group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables   clade_statistics <- tibble(       cluster_name = c("S1","S2"),       n_muts = c(m_clade,m_driver),       vaf_1_n = c(vaf_clade$vaf_1_n,vaf_driver$vaf_1_n),       vaf_1_p = c(vaf_clade$vaf_1_p,vaf_driver$vaf_1_p),       vaf_2_n = c(vaf_clade$vaf_2_n,vaf_driver$vaf_2_n),       vaf_2_p = c(vaf_clade$vaf_2_p,vaf_driver$vaf_2_p),       is_clade = c(TRUE,FALSE),       names = c("B","B"),       driver_type = c("dc","dc"),       has_driver = c(TRUE,TRUE),       rewind = c(FALSE,FALSE) )   times = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(sample) %>%    summarize(t = max(birth_time)) %>% pull(t) %>% sort()  counts = driver_example$counts  n_times = 2  c1 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[1] - 0.01 & time < times[1] + 0.01) c1 = c1[c(nrow(c1)-1,nrow(c1)),] c2 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[2] - 0.01 & time < times[2] + 0.01) c2 = c2[c(nrow(c2)-1,nrow(c2)),]  ztot  = c(c1 %>% pull(count) %>% sum(),c2 %>% pull(count) %>% sum())  rho_1 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_1") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_1_n = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_1_p = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  rho_2 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_2") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_2_n = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_2_p = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  zminus = c(ccf_1_n,ccf_2_n)*ztot zplus =  c(ccf_1_p,ccf_2_p)*ztot   counts <- tibble(   count_n = zminus,   count_p = zplus,   time = times )  mu = driver_example$mu$mean    genomic_constants <- tibble(   variable = c("genome_length", "mu"),   value = c(51e6, mu) )  pepi_obj = init(clade_statistics = clade_statistics,counts = counts,                 genomic_constants = genomic_constants)  pepi_obj #> $clade_statistics #> # A tibble: 2 × 11 #>   cluster_name n_muts vaf_1_n vaf_1_p vaf_2_n vaf_2_p is_clade names driver_type #>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <lgl>    <chr> <chr>       #> 1 S1              264  0.0474   0.294  0.0487   0.313 TRUE     B     dc          #> 2 S2              312  0.217    0.326  0.236    0.355 FALSE    B     dc          #> # ℹ 2 more variables: has_driver <lgl>, rewind <lgl> #>  #> $counts #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   count_n count_p  time #>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 195232.  75923.  14.4 #> 2 537863. 296465.  15.4 #>  #> $genomic_constants #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   variable        value #>   <chr>           <dbl> #> 1 genome_length 5.10e+7 #> 2 mu            4.81e-7 #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "PEPI"

title: PEPI: Inference example with a subclonal expansion
text: Driver-associated mutations form high-VAF cluster. cluster reaches higher VAF ⊕\oplus sample , time driver emergence, ⊕\oplus population smaller, driver therefore expands competing fewer cells. also observe distinct cluster associated first nested clade within driver lineage.
code: muts <- PEPI::driver_example$muts  get_branch = function(forest,cell_id,stop_id){      s = cell_id   branch = s      while(s > stop_id){          s =  forest %>% filter(cell_id == s) %>% pull(ancestor)     if(s > stop_id){branch = c(branch,s)}   }      return(branch)    }  id_B = forest %>% as_tibble() %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  id_cl = forest %>% as_tibble() %>% filter(mutant == "B",epistate == "+") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()  branch_dr = get_branch(forest,cell_id = id_B,stop = 0) branch_cl = get_branch(forest,cell_id = id_cl,stop = id_B)  muts = muts %>% mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id %in% branch_dr,"driver",     ifelse(cell_id %in% branch_cl,"first nested clade","subclonal"))) %>%   mutate(label = ifelse(cell_id == 0,"truncal",label))   p1 <- PEPI::plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_1_n", "vaf_1_p")) p2 <- PEPI::plot_vaf(muts, variables = c("vaf_2_n", "vaf_2_p")) ggarrange(plotlist= list(p1$scatterplots[[1]],p2$scatterplots[[1]]),nrow = 1, ncol = 2,common.legend = T)

title: PEPI: Inference example with a subclonal expansion
text: object requires clade statistics (number mutations, ccf), total cell counts different time points genomic constants mutation rate genomic length.
code: m_clade = muts %>% filter(label == "first nested clade") %>% nrow() m_driver = muts %>% filter(label == "driver") %>% nrow()  vaf_clade = muts %>% filter(label == "first nested clade") %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf")) %>%    reshape2::melt() %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables  vaf_driver = muts %>% filter(label == "driver",cell_id == id_B) %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("vaf"))%>%  reshape2::melt() %>% filter(value < Inf) %>%    group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>%    pivot_wider(names_from = variable,values_from = v) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables   clade_statistics <- tibble(       cluster_name = c("S1","S2"),       n_muts = c(m_clade,m_driver),       vaf_1_n = c(vaf_clade$vaf_1_n,vaf_driver$vaf_1_n),       vaf_1_p = c(vaf_clade$vaf_1_p,vaf_driver$vaf_1_p),       vaf_2_n = c(vaf_clade$vaf_2_n,vaf_driver$vaf_2_n),       vaf_2_p = c(vaf_clade$vaf_2_p,vaf_driver$vaf_2_p),       is_clade = c(TRUE,FALSE),       names = c("B","B"),       driver_type = c("dc","dc"),       has_driver = c(TRUE,TRUE),       rewind = c(FALSE,FALSE) )   times = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(sample) %>%    summarize(t = max(birth_time)) %>% pull(t) %>% sort()  counts = driver_example$counts  n_times = 2  c1 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[1] - 0.01 & time < times[1] + 0.01) c1 = c1[c(nrow(c1)-1,nrow(c1)),] c2 = counts %>% filter(time >= times[2] - 0.01 & time < times[2] + 0.01) c2 = c2[c(nrow(c2)-1,nrow(c2)),]  ztot  = c(c1 %>% pull(count) %>% sum(),c2 %>% pull(count) %>% sum())  rho_1 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_1") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_1_n = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_1_p = (rho_1 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_1 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  rho_2 = forest %>% filter(sample == "Sampling_2") %>% group_by(epistate) %>% summarize(n = length(cell_id)) ccf_2_n = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum()) ccf_2_p = (rho_2 %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))/(rho_2 %>% pull(n) %>% sum())  zminus = c(ccf_1_n,ccf_2_n)*ztot zplus =  c(ccf_1_p,ccf_2_p)*ztot   counts <- tibble(   count_n = zminus,   count_p = zplus,   time = times )  mu = driver_example$mu$mean    genomic_constants <- tibble(   variable = c("genome_length", "mu"),   value = c(51e6, mu) )  pepi_obj = init(clade_statistics = clade_statistics,counts = counts,                 genomic_constants = genomic_constants)  pepi_obj #> $clade_statistics #> # A tibble: 2 × 11 #>   cluster_name n_muts vaf_1_n vaf_1_p vaf_2_n vaf_2_p is_clade names driver_type #>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <lgl>    <chr> <chr>       #> 1 S1              264  0.0474   0.294  0.0487   0.313 TRUE     B     dc          #> 2 S2              312  0.217    0.326  0.236    0.355 FALSE    B     dc          #> # ℹ 2 more variables: has_driver <lgl>, rewind <lgl> #>  #> $counts #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   count_n count_p  time #>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 195232.  75923.  14.4 #> 2 537863. 296465.  15.4 #>  #> $genomic_constants #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   variable        value #>   <chr>           <dbl> #> 1 genome_length 5.10e+7 #> 2 mu            4.81e-7 #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "PEPI"

using all as measure variables pepi_obj <- PEPI::get_prior(pepi_obj) #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables #> No id variables; using all as measure variables p_omega <- PEPI::plot_inference(pepi_obj, parameter = c("omega_p"), log_scale = TRUE)  # Data frame for the line vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 5e-3)  # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping p_omega = p_omega +   geom_vline(data = vline_df,              aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),              linetype = "dashed") +   scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red")  p_s <- PEPI::plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("s_epi"), log_scale = F)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.3)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_s = p_s +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     )      p_sd <- PEPI::plot_inference(   pepi_obj,   parameter = c("s_dc[1]"), log_scale = F)      # Data frame for the line   vline_df <- data.frame(threshold = "Threshold", xval = 0.25)      # Add geom_vline with aesthetic mapping   p_sd = p_sd +     geom_vline(       data = vline_df,       aes(xintercept = xval, color = threshold),       linetype = "dashed"     ) +     scale_color_manual(name = "Ground truth", values = "red"     ) + xlim(0,1)  ggarrange(plotlist = list(p_omega,p_s,p_sd),nrow = 1,ncol = 3,common.legend = T) #> Warning: Removed 1745 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range #> (`stat_bin()`). #> Warning: Removed 4 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_bar()`).
